name: math_adjoint_pair

phase_0.boundary_condition: The category theory framework defining the relationship between two categories C and D.

VINIT.justification: The state before any objects or morphisms are defined.

TANCH.justification: The final state where the hom-set isomorphism is established and closed.

AFWD.justification: The covariant mapping from category C to category D.

AREV.justification: The mapping from category D back to category C.

CLINK.justification: The chaining of F and G to form endofunctors GF or FG.

IMSCRIB.justification: The functor that maps every object and morphism to itself.

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the mapping into the left-adjoint and right-adjoint perspectives.

FFUSE.justification: The natural isomorphism that identifies the two hom-sets as equivalent.

EVALT.justification: The natural transformation from identity to GF representing the insertion of the unit.

EVALF.justification: The natural transformation from FG to identity representing the evaluation of the counit.

ENGAGR.justification: The triangular identities where unit and counit coexist to define the adjunction.

IFIX.justification: The permanent entry of the adjoint pair into the mathematical catalog.

phase_3.both_description: The unit and counit satisfy the triangle identities simultaneously.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the mathematical space for categories C and D.
Define the identity functors for each category.
Establish the left adjoint functor F mapping C to D.
Establish the right adjoint functor G mapping D to C.
Compose F and G to form the endofunctor GF on category C.
Branch the morphism analysis into the D-target and C-source perspectives.
Apply the unit natural transformation η to the T-branch.
Apply the counit natural transformation ε to the F-branch.
Verify the zig-zag identities where both transformations hold the adjunction.
Reconstitute the hom-set isomorphism from the two branches.
Record the adjoint pair f ⊣ g in the permanent reference catalog.
Close the system boundary under the established adjunction.
